title: Xanthe and the Compass
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the interior, bush pilot Silas Pemberton is hired to fly a search party upriver—only to find the team's abandoned gear arranged like a message, and among the wreckage a brass compass belonging to his long-lost sister Xanthe, who disappeared years ago chasing rumors of an unregistered settlement of people fleeing unjust convictions. Silas joins forces with the survey team's sole survivor, cartographer Nia Okafor, and follows the river to its forbidden source before monsoon season seals the valley. There he finds Xanthe alive as the settlement's reluctant leader, but the government's real mission was to map the valley for eviction and resource seizure. In the climax, Silas burns his own plane's fuel caches and flies the settlement's evidence out through the storm's edge, forcing a public reckoning; the epilogue chapters show the community winning recognition on their own terms, with Silas choosing to stay—not as rescuer, but as family.
about_author: Theo Voss is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent a decade ferrying supplies to remote river communities before turning to fiction. Their novels blend aviation realism with stories about outsiders building justice where institutions failed.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, Rain
chapters.summary: Silas Pemberton's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes his world: unreliable radios, gossip as currency, and the approaching monsoon. He hears the first rumor of a vanished survey team and dismisses it. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness—he hasn't flown for anyone he loves in years.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A government liaison offers triple pay to fly a search party upriver before weather closes the passes. The paperwork feels wrong—sealed orders, no manifest for half the cargo. Silas signs anyway because debt doesn't care about instincts. Emotional beat: uneasy compromise, the first crack in his careful neutrality.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Nia Okafor's POV introduces her: the survey team's cartographer, grounded by a sprained ankle when her colleagues went missing, now insisting on returning. She and Silas circle each other warily over preflight checks. Emotional beat: two guarded professionals recognizing a shared refusal to be handled.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs during the flight. Storm cells build on the horizon as they follow the river gorge; radio chatter from other pilots goes strange, then silent. They spot something impossible below—a clearing that isn't on any map Nia drew herself. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The survey camp stands intact: tents pitched, instruments running, food untouched—but no people, no tracks, no struggle. Nia finds her own handwriting on a logbook page she never wrote, dated three days after the disappearance. Emotional beat: violation; the wilderness has been edited by human hands.

chapters.title: The Brass Compass
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, intimate flashback woven through present action. Wedged under the camp stove is a compass engraved with an X—the one he gave his sister Xanthe before she vanished seven years ago. His hands shake for the first time in the book. Emotional beat: grief reignited; the search just became personal.

chapters.title: What Nia Mapped
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Under pressure from the liaison's sealed orders, she confesses the survey's true purpose: not geology but reconnaissance for an eviction—a hidden valley flagged for seizure. Her guilt over leading her team there is raw. Emotional beat: confession as trust; the alliance becomes real.

chapters.title: Sealed Orders
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The liaison's deputy, Hargrove, orders them to abandon the search and fly out. Silas refuses, citing weather; really, he can't leave the compass behind. Hargrove quietly logs Silas's tail number. Emotional beat: the moment neutrality dies—Silas chooses a side without admitting it aloud.

chapters.title: River Country
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They travel upstream by boat, reading sign: cut saplings, smoke ghosts, a snare set by someone skilled. Nia teaches Silas to read water; Silas teaches Nia to read weather. Emotional beat: found-family warmth kindling between two people trained to need no one.

chapters.title: The Watcher
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Someone shadows them through the forest—deliberately visible once, then gone. That night their boat is moved but nothing stolen, a warning in the grammar of people who've survived raids. Emotional beat: fear tempered by respect; they're being tested, not hunted.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At a ridge above the river's source basin, they're taken at arrowpoint—and the archer lowers her bow when she sees Silas's face. Xanthe, older, harder, alive. The reunion is furious and tender at once: she thought he'd sold her out years ago. Emotional beat: joy laced with betrayal, neither sibling willing to apologize first.

chapters.title: The Valley of the Unlisted
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She leads them down into a concealed settlement of fugitives, debt-runners, and wrongly convicted families who erased themselves from every registry. She explains why she left: the law had made her a criminal for surviving. Emotional beat: wonder and unease—paradise built on permanent hiding.

chapters.title: The Survey Team Found
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The missing surveyors are here, alive but shaken—they'd discovered the valley's location in their own data and were detained by the settlement rather than risk exposure. One surveyor, Reyes, argues they should still report it. Emotional beat: moral deadlock; both sides have justice on their side.

chapters.title: Hargrove Arrives
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Hargrove's enforcement flight lands at the old survey camp downstream with armed contractors and eviction writs. The monsoon is forty-eight hours out. Silas realizes his plane is the only bridge between the valley and the outside. Emotional beat: trap closing; every option costs someone everything.

chapters.title: Council of the Erased
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The settlement debates: hide deeper, flee over the pass, or fight. Xanthe argues for a fourth path—exposure on their own terms, with evidence of the fraudulent surveys. Old wounds surface; some blame her leadership. Emotional beat: fracture within found family, the cost of leading the unwanted.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. To delay Hargrove, Silas drains and torches his own reserve fuel caches at the downstream strip, stranding the contractors' resupply. It's his livelihood burning. Nia covers his retreat and takes a graze wound. Emotional beat: costly commitment—he stops being a courier and becomes a partisan.

chapters.title: The Evidence Flight
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. They load the plane with forged survey documents, recorded confessions, and the settlement's registry of wrongful convictions. The monsoon wall looms black over the pass. Xanthe hands Silas the compass back: 'You always flew true. Fly this.' Emotional beat: farewell charged with hope instead of grief.

chapters.title: Through the Storm's Edge
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, near-single-scene tension. A white-knuckle flight along the monsoon's leading edge, engine coughing, instruments lying, Nia navigating by the river below. They clear the pass with minutes to spare and land hard at a coastal airstrip where a journalist waits. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The evidence detonates publicly: the survey fraud, the eviction scheme, the list of the wrongly convicted. Hargrove is suspended; hearings begin. But officials also demand the valley's coordinates, and Nia holds the only complete map. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by new leverage and new danger.

chapters.title: The Map Question
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Called to testify, Nia must choose between legal protection and protecting the settlement. She submits a doctored chart placing the valley thirty miles off, then resigns her commission. Emotional beat: quiet heroism; justice outside the law means accepting its penalties.

chapters.title: Recognition
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Government negotiators arrive—invited this time—to grant the valley provisional status as a self-governing commons. Some settlers don't trust it; Xanthe signs anyway, betting that visibility beats erasure. Emotional beat: cautious reconciliation; the found family risks becoming a real community.

chapters.title: Compass Rose
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, closing chapter. Months later, Silas flies supply runs to the valley openly, his tail number known to everyone. He and Xanthe repair what the years broke, slowly, over shared coffee at the strip. The compass sits on his dashboard, needle steady north. Emotional beat: homecoming—not to a place, but to people.
